ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Here is a Physoly round button badge, in which the logo is printed on the flat and rigid surface of this badge. Toss it in the air and track the motions of three points (indicated by cyan circles in the figure) separated a straight-line distance of $L=5 \mathrm{~mm}$ apart. At a particular moment, we find that these all have the same speed $V=4 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$ but are heading to different directions which form an angle of $\theta=30^{\circ}$ between each pair. Determine the then angular velocity of the badge (in $\left.\mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}\right)$.

The problem gives that the straight-line spacing that can be taken between these points is L = 5 mm, and at a certain instant the three points have the same speed but their directions have pairwise included angles of θ = 30°. Reasoning: According to the method draft, arbitrarily choose two cyan points separated by L. Their velocity magnitudes are both V, and the angle between their velocity directions is θ, therefore the magnitude of the relative velocity of the two velocity vectors is |v1 - v2| = 2V sin(θ/2). For planar rigid body motion, the magnitude of the relative velocity of two points is also equal to ωL, so ωL = 2V sin(θ/2). Substitute V = 4 cm/s = 40 mm/s, L = 5 mm, θ = 30°: ω = 2·40·sin(15°)/5 = 4.1411 rad/s.

raw_record.question_text: Here is a Physoly round button badge, in which the logo is printed on the flat and rigid surface of this badge. Toss it in the air and track the motions of three points (indicated by cyan circles in the figure) separated a straight-line distance of $L=5 \mathrm{~mm}$ apart. At a particular moment, we find that these all have the same speed $V=4 \mathrm{~cm} / \mathrm{s}$ but are heading in different directions which form an angle of $\theta=30^{\circ}$ between each pair. Determine the angular velocity of the badge (in $\mathrm{rad}/\mathrm{s}$).

method.method_draft: Read the figure as showing three tracked cyan points on a flat rigid badge. Pick any two points whose separation is the given straight-line distance L. The text gives their speed magnitude as V and says the directions of their velocity vectors differ by θ. For two equal-length vectors with included angle θ, the relative-speed magnitude is |v1-v2| = 2V sin(θ/2). For a rigid body in planar motion, the relative speed of two points also equals ωL. So ω = 2V sin(θ/2)/L. Convert V = 4 cm/s = 40 mm/s and use L = 5 mm, θ = 30°. Then ω = 2·40·sin15°/5 ≈ 4.1411 rad/s.

method.method_draft: Read the image as a rigid badge with three marked points moving on the same body. Interpret the motion instantaneously as pure rotation about an instantaneous center. Then each point’s speed satisfies V = ωr, where r is its distance to the instantaneous center. The angle between the velocity directions of two points is θ, so the corresponding radii to the instantaneous center are separated by the same angle θ. The distance between the two points is then the chord of a circle of radius r: L = 2r sin(θ/2). Solve for r = L/[2 sin(θ/2)] and substitute into ω = V/r to get ω = 2V sin(θ/2)/L. With V = 40 mm/s, L = 5 mm, θ = 30°, this gives ω ≈ 4.1411 rad/s.
